claims.statement: Finite weighted trace formula (2.1), quadratic generating operator (2.2), and conditional Chebyshev/variation bound (2.4).

The finite-pair derivative identity survives, but its full-grid trace and an infinite homogeneous-pair sum have different cutoff-order limits. Every trace-class observable of the homogeneous signed frame is depth-independent.
The old finite selected-block bound needs o(L^-2), not merely o(1), error to force a=L*delta to vanish. External-zero localization and single-vector tails are different obligations.

In the finite exact master-lattice mixed 0/1/2 model with multiplicity-one pairs and arbitrary site-dependent depths in [0,2*pi], ||G-G0||_F^2 <= Delta. A common depth or finite alphabet is unnecessary.

For arbitrary finite depths, ||G-G0||_F^2 <= Delta+2 B_high, with the explicit positive pair-versus-nonpair leakage in (4.4). Pure all-pair configurations have equality Delta=||G-2I||_F^2 without a depth cutoff.
For a d-row contraction, unit-atom short normalization is alpha^-1. The Hilbert-Schmidt discrepancy divided by sqrt(P) is at most sqrt(eta)/alpha, not sqrt(eta).

With critical mean load one, P divisible by four, moderate variable depths and the two exact ideal moment assumptions (6.2), s >= 2/3 + (sqrt(119/72)-sqrt(19/12))^2/4 = 0.666852966133... . This is not an unconditional zeta bound.

A weighted trace is not automatically a usable new independent depth channel, nor established as necessary: direct operator transfer bypasses depth classification in the specified model. It may still be useful with additional arithmetic/localization control.
